newsitem.title: USA: IMF has agreed broader debt relief guidelines.
newsitem.headline: IMF has agreed broader debt relief guidelines.

text.p: The IMF has agreed broad guidelines for deciding which countries qualify for new debt relief, which should allow Ivory Coast, Guyana, Yemen, Congo and Mauritania to benefit, Philippe Maystadt, head of the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee, said on Saturday.

He told reporters the guidelines would allow these countries to benefit from a new debt relief initiative in addition to those which meet a requirement that debt service costs are more than 200 to 250 percent of export earnings. All five have slightly lower debt to export ratios.

The debt relief initiative, to be carried out jointly by the International Monetary Fund, World Bank and Paris Club of creditor nations, is meant to reduce debt faced by the world's poor, heavily-indebted nations.

The IMF this week approved a debt relief plan for Uganda, the first to benefit from the new initiative. Maystadt said Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Ivory Coast were likely to follow in the next few weeks.
Altogether, some 15 to 20 countries should benefit from the debt relief initiative, which Maystadt estimated would cost between $5.5 billion and $8.4 billion.
He said the broadening of the guidelines for eligibility for debt relief would affect only a limited number of countries and would not add much to the total cost of the debt relief initiative.
"There are five countries concerned -- Ivory Coast, Guyana, Yemen, Congo and Mauritania," he said.
Maystadt, who is also Belgium's finance minister, was speaking to reporters ahead of full ministerial meetings of the IMF and World Bank, which are set to start on Monday.
